# count NaN for each column
count_na_per_column <- function(data) {
  sapply(data, function(col) sum(is.na(col)))}

count_na_per_column_df <- function(data) {
  na_counts <- sapply(data, function(col) sum(is.na(col)))
  na_counts_df <- data.frame(
    feature = names(na_counts),
    na_count = na_counts
  )
  na_counts_df %>% arrange(desc(na_count))
}

# extract first genre for the spotify genre
extract_first_genre <- function(df, genre_column = "spotify_genre") {
  # check if column exists
  if (!genre_column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", genre_column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  # removes useless not required characters
  df[[genre_column]] <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", df[[genre_column]])
  
  # create a list, with div = ,
  genre_list <- strsplit(df[[genre_column]], split = ",")
  
  # extract only the first genre for each line or rename "others"
  df$first_genre <- sapply(genre_list, function(x) {
    x <- trimws(x)  # remove blanks
    if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[1]) || x[1] == "") {
      return("others")
    } else {
      return(x[1])
    }
  })
  
  # convert to categorical value
  df$first_genre <- as.factor(df$first_genre)
  
  # output
  return(df)
}

# process and encode the genre column
process_and_encode_genre <- function(df, genre_column = "first_genre", top_n = 15) {
  # check if column exists
  if (!genre_column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", genre_column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  # count the frequency
  genre_counts <- table(df[[genre_column]])
  
  # put them in decrescent order
  genre_counts_sorted <- sort(genre_counts, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # take top N genres
  top_genres <- names(genre_counts_sorted)[1:min(top_n, length(genre_counts_sorted))]
  
  # rename not in top N into 'others'
  df[[genre_column]] <- ifelse(
    df[[genre_column]] %in% top_genres,
    df[[genre_column]],
    "others"
  )
  
  # convert
  df[[genre_column]] <- as.factor(df[[genre_column]])
  
  # remove original column
  if ("spotify_genre" %in% colnames(df)) {
    df <- subset(df, select = -c(spotify_genre))
  }
  
  # create dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
  dummy <- dummyVars(paste("~", genre_column), data = df)
  dummy_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))
  
  final_df <- bind_cols(
    df %>% select(-all_of(genre_column)),
    dummy_df
  )
  
  # output
  return(final_df)
}

# encode popularity column
encode_spotify_popularity <- function(df, column = "spotify_track_popularity") {
  # check if column exists
  if (!column %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop(paste("La colonna", column, "non esiste nel dataframe"))
  }
  
  categorize_popularity <- function(x) {
    if (is.na(x)) return(NA)
    if (x <= 25) {
      return("low")
    } else if (x <= 50) {
      return("medium")
    } else if (x <= 75) {
      return("high")
    } else if (x <= 100) {
      return("very high")
    } else {
      return(NA)  # out of range
    }
  }
  
  df[[column]] <- sapply(df[[column]], categorize_popularity)
  
  # convert in ordered factor
  df[[column]] <- factor(df[[column]], 
                         levels = c("low", "medium", "high", "very high"), 
                         ordered = TRUE)
  
  # output
  return(df)
}

# plots the confusion matrix
plot_conf_matrix <- function(conf_matrix_object, title = "Confusion Matrix") {
  
  # converts confusion matrix into dataframe
  cm_df <- as.data.frame(conf_matrix_object$table)
  
  # find columns names (Truth, Prediction, Freq)
  colnames(cm_df) <- tolower(colnames(cm_df)) # rende tutto minuscolo
  
  # rename them
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) %in% c("reference", "truth")] <- "Actual"
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) == "prediction"] <- "Predicted"
  names(cm_df)[names(cm_df) %in% c("freq", "n")] <- "Freq"
  
  # plot
  p <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 5, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Predicted Class",
         y = "Actual Class",
         fill = "Count") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
  
  return(p)
}

3.1 Aggregations

# new features creation
billboard_summary <- billboard %>%
  group_by(song_id) %>%
  summarise(
    min_position = min(week_position),
    max_position = max(week_position),
    avg_position = mean(week_position),
    weeks_in_chart = n_distinct(week_id),
    final_position = last(week_position)
  )

full_data_aggregate <- merge(billboard_summary, audio_features, by = "song_id", all = FALSE)
full_data_aggregate <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c(instrumentalness, time_signature))

4 Main Question - Given the audio features of a new song, will it become popular?

4.1 Regression - predict the position on the billboard

Preprocessing

Remove unrelevant features

regression_data <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c(song_id, min_position, max_position, avg_position, weeks_in_chart, final_position))
print(head(regression_data,5))

One hot encoding of the 15 most frequent genre

regression_data <- extract_first_genre(regression_data)
regression_data_encoded <- process_and_encode_genre(regression_data, top_n = 15)
set.seed(45)

Scaling

regression_data_encoded_scaled <- robustHD::standardize(regression_data_encoded |> select(-spotify_track_popularity))

regression_data_encoded_scaled['spotify_track_popularity'] = regression_data$spotify_track_popularity

print(head(regression_data_encoded_scaled, 5))

Regressions

  1. split the dataset
set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(head(regression_data_encoded,n_samples_to_consider), prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# resampling for cross validation
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_data, v = 5)
  1. define recipe, models and workflows
# recipe
recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

# models with tuning parameters
task = 'regression'
models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 500) |>
    set_engine("randomForest") |> set_mode(task),
  
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = tune(), learn_rate = tune()) |>
    set_engine("xgboost") |> set_mode(task),
  
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune()) |>
    set_engine("kknn") |> set_mode(task)
)

# workflows
workflows_list <- purrr::imap(models, function(model, name) {
  workflow() |> add_model(model) |> add_recipe(recipe_spec)
})
  1. tuning
# tune_race_anova
tuned_models <- purrr::imap(workflows_list, function(wf, name) {
  tune_race_anova(
    wf,
    resamples = cv_folds,
    grid = 5,
    metrics = metric_set(rmse),
    control = control_race(verbose_elim = TRUE)
  )})
ℹ Evaluating against the initial 3 burn-in resamples.
ℹ Racing will minimize the rmse metric.
ℹ Resamples are analyzed in a random order.
G3;ℹ Fold5: 0 eliminated; 5 candidates remain.
gG3;ℹ Fold3: 0 eliminated; 5 candidates remain.
gℹ Evaluating against the initial 3 burn-in resamples.
ℹ Racing will minimize the rmse metric.
ℹ Resamples are analyzed in a random order.
G3;ℹ Fold4: 1 eliminated; 4 candidates remain.
gG3;ℹ Fold5: All but one parameter combination were eliminated.
gℹ Evaluating against the initial 3 burn-in resamples.
ℹ Racing will minimize the rmse metric.
ℹ Resamples are analyzed in a random order.
G3;ℹ Fold4: 2 eliminated; 3 candidates remain.
gG3;ℹ Fold5: 0 eliminated; 3 candidates remain.
g
# extract best values
best_models <- purrr::map(tuned_models, ~ select_best(.x))
G2;H2;Warningh in select_best(.x) :
  No value of `metric` was given; "rmse" will be used.g
G2;H2;Warningh in select_best(.x) :
  No value of `metric` was given; "rmse" will be used.g
G2;H2;Warningh in select_best(.x) :
  No value of `metric` was given; "rmse" will be used.g
  1. finalize and fits the models to the training set
final_models <- purrr::map2(workflows_list, best_models, ~ finalize_workflow(.x, .y) |> fit(data = train_data))
  1. evaluation on the test set
results <- purrr::map(final_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) |>
    bind_cols(test_data) |>
    metrics(truth = spotify_track_popularity, estimate = .pred)})

# summary RMSE
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model") |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |> arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
all_predictions <- purrr::imap(final_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) |>
    bind_cols(test_data) |>
    mutate(model = .y)
}) |> bind_rows()

ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = spotify_track_popularity, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predictions vs Real Values for Models",
    x = "Real Values (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predictions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

features importance

# VIP plot list
vip_plots <- list()

# Random Forest
rf_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(final_models$rf)
if (inherits(rf_fit$fit, "randomForest")) {
  vip_plots$rf <- vip(rf_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("Random Forest - Variable Importance")
}

# XGBoost
xgb_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(final_models$xgb)
if (inherits(xgb_fit$fit, "xgb.Booster")) {
  vip_plots$xgb <- vip(xgb_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("XGBoost - Variable Importance")
}

6. Have songs from the last ten years become louder than before? We chose to perform this hypothesis test on the loudness because we noticed it was the most important feature among all the audio features of the songs.

6.1 Hypothesis test

Preprocessing

hypothesis_data_before <- data_filtered_before_encoded |> select(where(is.numeric))

  select(1:(ncol(hypothesis_data_after) - 11))

  select(1:(ncol(hypothesis_data_before) - 11))

After 2000

#plotting the QQ plots to show the distribution of the dataset
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
for (colname in names(numeric_data_before_no_genre)) {
  qqnorm(numeric_data_before_no_genre[[colname]], main = paste("QQ Plot -", colname))
  qqline(numeric_data_before_no_genre[[colname]])
}

Based on the QQ plots for the periods before and after 2015, none of the feature distributions appear to be normal. Therefore, to compare the two distributions, we should use the Wilcoxon test.

Hypothesis Test

#Doing a wilcox test based on the loudness of the songs
wilcox.test(
  hypothesis_data_after$loudness,
  hypothesis_data_before$loudness,
  alternative = "greater"
)

    Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  hypothesis_data_after$loudness and hypothesis_data_before$loudness
W = 130673989, p-value < 2.2e-16
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is greater than 0
#filtering the datasets with only the loudness feature
loudness_after <- hypothesis_data_after$loudness
loudness_before <- hypothesis_data_before$loudness


plot(density(loudness_after), col = "blue", lwd = 2,
     main = "Loudness Density: After 2000 vs Before 2000", xlab = "Loudness")
lines(density(loudness_before), col = "red", lwd = 2)

legend("topright", legend = c("After 2000", "Before 2000"), col = c("blue", "red"), lwd = 2)

As we can see from the two distributions, songs released after 2015 are louder than those released before. Why is that? This could be due to the evolution of music over the years—listeners’ tastes have changed, and artists have explored new styles, adapting their sound to the cultural and historical context.

Question 2 - As a manager, should I continue to invest in this song given its statistics? Will it remain popular over time?

Regression - predict the position on the Billboard

Preprocessing

Remove unrelevant features

regression_data <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c(song_id))
print(head(regression_data,5))

one hot encoding of the most 15 important genres

regression_data <- extract_first_genre(regression_data)
regression_data_encoded <- process_and_encode_genre(regression_data, top_n = 15)
print(head(regression_data_encoded, 5))

Regression

set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(head(regression_data_encoded,100), prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# recipe
recipe_spec <- recipe(final_position ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

task = 'regression'

# models
models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = 5) %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode(task),
  #lm = linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% set_mode(task),
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 100, tree_depth = 10) %>% set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode(task),
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = 5) %>% set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode(task)
)

# workflow
workflows_list <- purrr::map(models, ~ workflow() %>% add_model(.x) %>% add_recipe(recipe_spec))

# train models
fitted_models <- purrr::map(workflows_list, ~ fit(.x, data = train_data))

# evaluation
results <- purrr::map(fitted_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = final_position, estimate = .pred)
})

# results
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model")

results_df %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
results <- list()

for (model_name in names(fitted_models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  wf <- workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
  
  fit_model <- fit(wf, data = train_data)
  
  preds <- predict(fit_model, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  results[[model_name]] <- preds
}

all_predictions <- bind_rows(results)

ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = final_position, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predictions vs Real Values per Modello",
    x = "Real Values (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predictions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# VIP plot list
vip_plots <- list()

# Random Forest
rf_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(fitted_models$rf)
if (inherits(rf_fit$fit, "randomForest")) {
  vip_plots$rf <- vip(rf_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("Random Forest - Variable Importance")
}

# XGBoost
xgb_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(fitted_models$xgb)
if (inherits(xgb_fit$fit, "xgb.Booster")) {
  vip_plots$xgb <- vip(xgb_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("XGBoost - Variable Importance")
}

# visualize plots
library(patchwork)

# show them
if (length(vip_plots) == 2) {
  vip_plots$rf + vip_plots$xgb
} else {
  # if only one is possible
  vip_plots[[1]]
}

Classification- predict whether a sign will be in the top 30

Preprocessing

classification_data <- full_data_aggregate |> select(-c( song_id))
print(head(classification_data,5))

Encode popularity

classification_data <- encode_spotify_popularity(classification_data)

classification_data <- classification_data |>
  filter(!is.na(spotify_track_popularity))

Encode genre

classification_data <- extract_first_genre(classification_data)
classification_data <- process_and_encode_genre(classification_data, top_n = 5)
#print number of NaN for each column
count_na_per_column_df(classification_data)
#create the new variable top30: whether a song is in the top 30
classification_data <- classification_data |>
  mutate(top30 = ifelse(final_position <= 30, 1, 0))
# remove final_position
classification_data <- classification_data |> select(-c( final_position))
print(head(classification_data,5))
# select only numerical data
numeric_data_clss <- classification_data |>
  select(where(is.numeric))

# correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data_clss, use = "complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, 
           method = "square",     # or "circle"
           type = "lower",        # only lower triangle        
           colors = c("red", "white", "blue"),
           title = "Correlation Matrix",
           ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal())

hist(classification_data$top30)

Classification

set.seed(42)
classification_data$top30 <- as.factor(classification_data$top30)
spotify_train_test <- classification_data |> initial_split(prop =  0.7)
spotify_train <- training(spotify_train_test) 
spotify_test  <- testing(spotify_train_test)
rand_forest_spec <- 
  rand_forest(mtry = 5, trees = 200) |>  
  set_engine('randomForest') |> 
  set_mode('classification')

rf_recipe = recipe(top30~.,
                   data=spotify_train)

rf_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) |> 
  add_model(rand_forest_spec)

rf_wf_fit <- rf_wf |> 
  fit(spotify_train)

rf_wf_fit
